title: TCP 三次握手与四次挥手：序号演算与状态迁移
expected_output:
=== TCP three-way handshake ===
client ISN x=1000, server ISN y=5000
  1) C -> S  SYN=1            seq=1000
  2) S -> C  SYN=1,ACK=1      seq=5000  ack=1001
  3) C -> S  ACK=1            seq=1001  ack=5001
  client state: CLOSED -> SYN_SENT -> ESTABLISHED
  server state: LISTEN -> SYN_RCVD -> ESTABLISHED
  SYN consumes 1 sequence number, so next data seq is ISN+1

=== TCP four-way teardown ===
  1) C -> S  FIN=1,ACK=1      seq=2000  ack=6000
  2) S -> C  ACK=1                  ack=2001   <- HALF-CLOSED
  3) S -> C  FIN=1,ACK=1      seq=9000  ack=2001
  4) C -> S  ACK=1                  ack=9001   then TIME_WAIT 2*MSL
  FIN also consumes 1 sequence number
  4 steps because TCP is FULL-DUPLEX: my FIN does not mean you are done
  if the server has nothing left to send, steps 2 and 3 merge -> looks like 3 steps

=== why TIME_WAIT = 2*MSL ===
  1) the last ACK might be lost; the peer will retransmit FIN and we must still be here
  2) leftover segments of the old connection must die before a new connection reuses
     the same 4-tuple (srcIP, srcPort, dstIP, dstPort)

=== why 3-way handshake (not 2) ===
  prevents a DELAYED duplicate SYN from an old, already-closed connection
  from creating a half-open connection on the server (server would wait forever)
  also confirms BOTH directions: send + receive capability of each side

=== RST and half-open ===
  peer sends SYN to a closed port -> reply RST (connection refused)
  SYN flood: attacker never sends the 3rd ACK -> SYN_RCVD queue fills
  defense: SYN cookies (do not allocate state until the handshake completes)
